technical_and_design_decisions: The user stories refer to Spring XD (a Spring sibling project that became Spring Cloud Data Flow) rather than Spring Framework core; references like 'modules.yml', 'xd-container-logger.properties' and the publish-maven script confirm this context.
Gradle is the build tool of choice (publish-maven.gradle, build.gradle references); Scala support is added via the Gradle Scala plugin.
Spark batch/streaming jobs are packaged as XD modules and deployed via the XD Admin/Container runtime; a Scala-compiled module will be treated as a regular zip-style module artifact.
The wiki is treated as the existing project wiki (GitHub/Confluence) where a new 'Troubleshooting' section will be added; no new doc tooling is introduced.
Kafka tests will be split into two complementary execution modes: a separate-server-process mode for fast local builds and an external-broker mode for CI/QA, both reusing the same test code base.
publish-maven.gradle will be refactored to load Spring Boot, hadoop-common and similar versions from dependencies.properties at build time; the build script will fail fast if a key is missing.
Sonar violations are addressed with the existing SonarQube instance: relevant ones are fixed in code, irrelevant ones are marked as 'Won't Fix' or 'False Positive' with a justification comment.
The Spark batch sample is delivered as a new module under the samples directory, built by Gradle, with a small unit/integration test suite and a short README.
assumptions: A single senior Java/Scala developer with prior Spring XD and Spark experience performs all work; effort is in 8-hour workdays.
Build environment (JDK 8, Gradle, Scala, Kafka, Spark, Sonar access, CI account) is already provisioned and reachable.
Access to source repository, wiki editing rights and SonarQube project are already granted.
User stories are independent enough to be worked on roughly in order U1..U8, with the common activities (design, integration, QA) wrapping the lot.
No new infrastructure (new CI nodes, new Sonar licenses, new Kafka clusters) is required.

U2/U3 are documentation/tiny-config changes that do not require new tests; U4/U6 share the same test code base so the Kafka test refactor effort is counted once under U4 and only configuration/doc work is counted under U6.
Sonar 'current violations' is assumed to be a tractable backlog (roughly 60-120 issues) for the project; 5 days is enough to triage and fix the relevant ones.
Integration testing runs against the existing local single-node XD/Spark/Kafka dev runtime; no long-running soak or performance tests are implied by the spec.

activities.activity_description: Read each user story, inspect the relevant code paths in the Spring XD repo (modules, build scripts, logger config, Kafka test harness, Spark samples), and produce a short design note covering approach, files to touch and test strategy for U1-U8.

activities.activity_name: U1 - Scala Spark Streaming module deployment support
activities.activity_description: Add Scala support to the relevant module(s)/build (Scala plugin, Scala/Java mixed compilation), package a Scala-based Spark streaming module, and verify it deploys end-to-end through the XD runtime so a Scala developer can deploy it without manual steps.

activities.activity_name: U2 - Wiki Troubleshooting section with recommended ulimit
activities.activity_description: Add a new 'Troubleshooting' section to the project wiki documenting the recommended ulimit setting of 10K for a distributed XD setup, including the FileNotFoundException / 'Too many open files' symptom and the reason to increase it.

Update the log pattern in config/xd-container-logger.properties to include the date (and where useful, milliseconds and timezone) so users can correlate log lines with a specific day and time during troubleshooting.

activities.activity_name: U4 - Refactor Kafka tests to use a separate Kafka server process
activities.activity_description: Refactor the Kafka integration test harness so the Kafka server is started/stopped as a separate OS process (or external test container) instead of in-JVM. Add/adjust Gradle tasks and documentation so developers can run the Kafka tests quickly on their workstation.

activities.activity_name: U5 - Refactor publish-maven.gradle to use dependencies.properties
activities.activity_description: Modify publish-maven.gradle to read Spring Boot, hadoop-common and other dependency versions from dependencies.properties instead of hard-coding them. Add validation, ensure the existing 'publish to Maven' flow still works, and document the new behavior.

activities.activity_name: U6 - Run Kafka tests on an external broker
activities.activity_description: Add a configuration profile/doc to the Kafka test suite so the same tests can be pointed at an external Kafka broker (e.g. via system properties/Gradle properties) to keep the build footprint small, and update developer docs accordingly.

activities.activity_name: U7 - Review and remediate Sonar violations
activities.activity_description: Run the SonarQube analysis, go through the current violations, fix the ones that are relevant in the source, and mark the irrelevant ones as 'Won't Fix' or 'False Positive' with a justification. Re-run the analysis to confirm the backlog is reduced.

activities.activity_name: U8 - Build Spark batch job sample
activities.activity_description: Create a runnable Spark batch job sample under the samples directory (Scala or Java + Spark APIs), wire it into the Gradle build, add a small test and a README showing how to launch it on the distributed runtime, demonstrating distributed data computation.

Run the full build with the new Spark module, the refactored publish script, the new Kafka test modes and the new Spark batch sample against a local XD/Spark/Kafka dev runtime, fix any regressions and confirm all user stories pass acceptance scenarios.

activities.activity_name: Code review, documentation polish and release preparation
activities.activity_description: Self/peer code review of all changes, final wiki/READMEs touch-up, update release notes for the new features and samples, and prepare the pull requests / release artifacts for the increment.
